before.title: Power Sliding Door Cable Failure
before.description: The power sliding door cable on the Metris is prone to fraying and snapping, leaving the door stuck open or closed. This is a common fleet complaint and typically occurs between 40,000-80,000 miles due to repeated cycling and poor cable routing.
before.solution: Replace the sliding door cable assembly. Use updated Mercedes part to reduce recurrence. Lubricate the cable tracks every 10,000 miles with dry silicone spray to extend cable life.
symptoms: Warning message on dash for sliding door malfunction

citations.title: MBWorld.org — Metris sliding door cable failure reports from fleet operators

communityRecommendations.content: Lubricate the sliding door track and cable guides with dry silicone spray every 10,000 miles. Avoid slamming the door manually when the power function is engaged — it stresses the cable.

proposal.title: Power Sliding Door Cable Failure
proposal.description: The reviewed Metris corpus does not establish power-sliding-door cable fraying or snapping across model years 2016-2023. Communication 10136064 concerns sliding-door noise, 10168261 a 2019 crack inspection, and 11034417 false door-ajar warnings caused by contact-plate or contact-switch paths. None identifies cable routing, a 40,000-80,000-mile failure window or a universal updated cable assembly.
proposal.solution: Document whether the door is stuck, noisy, cracked or falsely reported open. Inspect door alignment, rollers and track, cable and drive unit, contact plate and switches, wiring and latch separately under the VIN-specific Mercedes procedure. Do not buy a cable assembly, drive unit, roller or contact plate from this page; the failed component and fitment are unresolved.
symptoms: door position and warning state documented
cable, drive and contact-switch paths separated

before.title: Harsh Shifting and Delayed Engagement in 7G-Tronic Transmission
before.description: The 7G-Tronic automatic transmission in the Metris exhibits harsh shifts, particularly the 2-3 and 4-5 upshifts, along with delayed engagement when shifting from park to drive. The issue worsens as the transmission fluid ages and the valve body accumulates debris from clutch material.
before.solution: Perform a full transmission fluid and filter change using MB-approved 236.14 specification fluid. If harsh shifting persists, the valve body may need replacement or rebuild. A transmission software update from Mercedes can recalibrate shift points and improve shift quality.
symptoms: Delayed engagement from Park to Drive

citations.title: MBWorld.org — Metris 7G-Tronic harsh shift complaints and transmission service intervals

communityRecommendations.content: Change transmission fluid every 40,000 miles rather than the factory "lifetime" interval. Use only MB 236.14 spec fluid. This alone resolves the harsh shifting in most cases.

proposal.title: Harsh Shifting and Delayed Engagement in 7G-Tronic Transmission
proposal.description: The reviewed Metris corpus does not establish recurring harsh 2-to-3 and 4-to-5 shifts or delayed Park-to-Drive engagement from aged fluid and clutch debris across model years 2016-2023. Communication 11023982 instead concerns loss of communication with the 722.9 VGS and requires power, connector, wiring and pin checks before any EHS replacement. It does not support a universal fluid service, valve-body rebuild or software recalibration for the frozen complaint.
proposal.solution: Record the exact shift or engagement event, temperature, load, delay and every VGS fault with freeze-frame and adaptation data. Verify fluid level and condition and test VGS communication, power, ground, connector pins and wiring before selecting a repair. Do not buy fluid, a filter, valve body or transmission controller from this page; the frozen condition and fitment are unresolved.
symptoms: exact shift and operating state documented
VGS faults and adaptation data preserved
fluid, communication and mechanical paths separated
